speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help me understand your sudden abdominal pain, can you tell me exactly where the pain is located and rate its severity on a scale of 1 to 10? Also, have you experienced any nausea, vomiting, or changes in your bowel movements recently?

speaker: Patient
text: 74-year-old male. The patient presents with sudden onset of abdominal pain around the umbilicus 16 hours ago, with recent history of hospitalization for an acute myocardial infarction a week ago. Reports several episodes of bloody loose bowel movements. Denies vomiting.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your recent heart attack and the sudden onset of periumbilical pain with bloody stools, I am highly concerned for mesenteric ischemia. I will immediately order imaging to assess blood flow to your intestines. REQUEST TEST: CT Angiography of the Abdomen and Pelvis

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Evidence suggestive of reduced blood flow to the mesenteric arteries.

speaker: Doctor
text: The CT findings confirm reduced mesenteric blood flow, which is consistent with acute mesenteric ischemia. Given your recent myocardial infarction and the presence of bloody stools, this is a surgical emergency. DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute Mesenteric Ischemia
